title: Thinking Short and Right Over Thinking Long: Serving LLM Reasoning Efficiently and Accurately
technique: SART: redundant branch sampling with early stopping plus two-phase dynamic pruning of low-reward branches (PRM), integrated with continuous batching

optimized_metrics.evidence: we prioritize right-thinking branches and release the resources consumed by the others on the fly, so that we can reduce the queuing latency effectively
managing the LLM reasoning processes to be short and right for efficiency and accuracy.

headline_claim.text: SART not only improves the accuracy of LLM reasoning but also enhances the serving efficiency, outperforming existing methods by up to 28.2× and on average 15.7× in terms of efficiency when achieving the same level of accuracy.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the end-to-end latency of a request includes queuing latency (the time spent waiting for batch availability) and inference latency (the time for prefilling and decoding).
metric_definitions.notes: Request = one reasoning question with N sampled branches; E2E latency is to the final ensembled response, so request-level here means per user question, not per single LLM sample. Not a PROGRAM_JCT in the multi-call sense.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: P97 latency corresponds to the maximum latency within which 97% of the requests are served.
metric_definitions.notes: Unusual tail percentile (P97) as primary efficiency metric.

metric_definitions.term_as_written: inference latency (E2E latency excluding queuing delay)
metric_definitions.definition_quote: end-to-end (E2E) latency and inference latency (i.e., E2E latency excluding queuing delay)
we measure each method’s effectiveness by calculating the accuracy (i.e., the ratio of correctly answered requests)
metric_definitions.notes: Accuracy of the ensembled final answer; part of the joint objective.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: outperforming existing methods by up to 28.2× and on average 15.7× in terms of efficiency when achieving the same level of accuracy
metric_definitions.notes: Efficiency = latency (percentile) at matched accuracy; not defined as a separate scalar.

load_regime: request-rate sweep at two arrival rates (1 and 4 req/s), sweep of branch count N
tradeoff_acknowledged: Larger N lowers inference latency but raises queuing delay and E2E latency; N in {4,8} has higher average (P50) and P90 latency than N in {1,2} but much lower P97/P99. SART accuracy slightly lower than Self-Consistency in several cases.
workloads: GPQA and GAOKAO, arrival 1 and 4 req/s
extractor_notes: Reasoning-serving: accuracy IS part of the objective (latency at matched accuracy; accuracy-vs-latency plots), and it is a two-sided claim (improve both). No TTFT/TPOT/throughput. Percentile latency is the headline efficiency metric. | TAIL AUDIT 2026-10-06: E2E tail stat -> n/a (metric targeted, percentile only reported)

tail_audit.correction: Demote E2E P97 'objective' to reported (it is the evaluation metric). Design aims: shorter reasoning branches, less queueing, same accuracy. Note: tail is the headline eval metric, and SART lowers P97/P99 as N grows, but no tail term in design.
